the spatial articulation of power and the manner in which it is inscribed in the built environment.
how the spatial production of power has been used in the past and how it is being used in the present to create a «Glocal Galician» identity.
how the spatial articulation of power is manifested in the materiality of the city and its surroundings, and the ways in which the city is used as a tool for the construction of a new identity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the «Glocal Galician» is an expression that, on one hand, is the product of the local and the global and, on the other hand, is an expression that has the power to transcend the local and the regional.
the «Glocal Galician» is a product of an interplay between a local and a global.
, as a whole, the Galician case study is a clear example of the way in which a local identity is constructed through the use of global cultural capital.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cidade da cultura de Galicia is the result of the articulation of power in Galicia.
the Camino de Compostela is a globalized space that has been glocalized in order to become the Cidade da Culture de Galicia.
the Cidade da cultura, like the Cathedral of Santiago de Compostel, is a globalized space that is at the same time a local space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the «Glocal» can only be fully understood by examining the ways in which localities, and the people who inhabit them, are shaped by and shape global processes.
these architectural enterprises, as well as the urban and political projects that accompany them, have been used to articulate power in a global context, but also in a local one.
the «Glocal» is not an abstract notion, but a concrete, material, and historical reality.
